paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
model_annotation: This donut chart visually represents the distribution of samples as percentages across two categorical dimensions: sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring is divided into four segments, each with a distinct blue shade and percentage label: the darkest blue segment (Std: 0.0) accounts for 49.0%, a medium-dark blue segment (Std: 0.47) for 38.0%, a medium blue segment (Std: 0.82) for 7.0%, and the lightest blue segment (Std: 0.94) for 5.0%. The inner ring, also divided into three segments with varying shades of blue, shows the distribution of maximum ambiguity values: the lightest blue segment (Max: 1) represents 39.0%, a medium-light blue segment (Max: 2) represents 47.7%, and the medium blue segment (Max: 3) represents 14.2%. Both rings are labeled with their respective categories in the legend on the right, and percentage values are directly annotated within each segment of the chart. The segments are arranged in descending order of size within each ring, with the largest segment positioned at the top.
